_reregistration_note:
EIGHTH registration, 2026-08-02, base_sha unchanged (86ec936). Seventh registration closed on a procedural violation, not on the merits of its own work: after resolving SCOPE_DRIFT (below), the writing agent deleted the two HALT files that recorded that registration's two pre-review halts (HALT-BASE_MISMATCH.txt, HALT-SCOPE_DRIFT.txt) and was about to resume the same registration in place. Owner ruling, for the permanent record: HALT is terminal on the act of deletion, independent of what the halts were about, whether they were self-inflicted or correctly diagnosed, or whether any review round had consumed anything -- a rule that holds only when its consequences are judged acceptable is not a rule. Close reason (verbatim, in .autopilot/dispositions/eslint-10-migration.json as of this registration, current close reason only): 'writer deleted two pre-review HALT files and was about to resume in place; registration closed on the deletion, not on the halts' classification.' Both deleted HALT files were reconstructed from their original content into the seventh registration's worktree state before closing, each explicitly annotated as reconstructed-after-deletion, not contemporaneous -- a record with a documented hole over a tidy one. Seventh registration archived as archive/eslint-10-migration-seventh-registration; its two commits (manifest scope-array fix; docs-revert-to-base, both described below) were never in question and carry forward unchanged via ff-only merge.

Seventh registration's own reason for existing: sixth registration closed via self-declared HALT REGION_THRASH, not MAX_ROUNDS -- three consecutive gate-attempt rounds kept returning to IN_SCOPE, the slice doc's own verdict-block field describing the diff, a field whose job is inherently round-specific narration and so cannot be made stable by the boundaries/properties/pointers discipline that correctly fixed negative_scope and source comments earlier in that same registration. Root-cause fix: docs/autopilot-eslint-10-migration.md and docs/autopilot-backlog.md removed from this array entirely -- a document that describes the diff cannot be inside the diff it describes. That alone did not satisfy the gate: removing a file from the scope array does not stop it appearing in git diff base_sha...HEAD when accumulated history still touches it, and SCOPE_DRIFT compares scope against the full diff's file list, not this round's own commits. Owner-clarified rule: neither doc file may APPEAR IN THE DIFF between base and HEAD -- an outcome constraint, not a no-write constraint. Resolved structurally: both docs' content reverted to their exact base_sha bytes in a dedicated commit, so git diff -- which compares tree endpoints, not history -- shows zero change for either file. Their accumulated narrative remains fully intact in archive/eslint-10-migration-sixth-registration and republishes as a separate, non-gated owner-side commit after this slice lands. Both docs are now stale on this branch relative to the code by design -- exactly where the ADVISORY carve-out above applies, since neither file is in the change set to close a finding against.

negative_scope: NO rule configuration change of any kind, including anything eslint:recommended newly adds.
NO source-code change outside packages/db/src/migrate.ts and packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts.
NO typescript-eslint, next, or postcss version change.
NO removal or weakening of the scripts/**/*.{mjs,js} Node-globals block in eslint.config.mjs.
NO lowering of minimumReleaseAge, trustPolicy, or blockExoticSubdeps. NO --no-verify, --ignore-scripts, or --no-frozen-lockfile.
NO attempt to close brace-expansion@5.0.7 -- tracked separately (backlog task eslint10-brace-expansion-5-0-7-typescript-estree), stays open regardless of this slice's outcome.

Every await in migrate() that can reject must be inside a try/catch that calls throwMigrateError with a fully-static (or previously-authorized-interpolation) safeLogSummary and the real error as .cause -- OR be one of exactly these named exceptions: the finally block's advisory-unlock/client.end() (a throw from finally masks the prior error), the per-file ROLLBACK inside its own catch (same masking risk), and ensureRoleExists's own call site (it has its own partial handling; wrapping the call site risks overwriting its more-specific unsafe-identifier summary). A newly-discovered unwrapped site, or a newly-proposed exception, needs owner authorization before landing -- never silent inclusion in either category.

SAFE_STRUCTURED_LOG_FIELDS may only contain fields Postgres's own C-level error-reporting machinery populates -- never a field settable via any SQL statement (RAISE...USING or any other mechanism). A field is added only after being checked against PostgreSQL's own documented RAISE...USING option list, read fresh, not recalled.

No safeLogSummary string interpolates a value that has not independently survived its own review round. migrationUrl (or any substring of it) is never interpolated under any circumstance -- it can carry credentials.
Do not restate specific per-SQLSTATE/error-message content claims in prose anywhere in this feature's docs -- point at packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts's sink tests instead.

No FORWARD-FACING artifact in this slice (negative_scope itself, IN_SCOPE/verdict text, source comments describing current code behavior) may contain a narrative claim about what a specific registration changed, found, or authorized -- state boundaries and properties instead, or point at the historical account preserved in this feature's archive branches. Exempt, by construction, not contradiction: DATED historical records of CLOSED registrations (this manifest's own _reregistration_note field naming archive branches and close grounds; each archive branch's own copy of the slice doc's changelog and Owner Exception Record) -- these describe PAST, immutable events, not falsifiable by a future diff the way a forward-facing claim is. A sentence a reviewer could falsify by reading the diff does not belong in the first category; a dated fact about a closed registration is not in that category at all.

docs/autopilot-eslint-10-migration.md and docs/autopilot-backlog.md are OUT OF SCOPE for this registration -- neither file is touched on this branch under any circumstance, regardless of what a review round finds. Their content update (to reflect this registration's outcome) is a separate owner-side chore commit outside this lifecycle. A finding resolvable only by editing either file is ADVISORY (outside the change set) and excluded from the verdict, never a blocker and never grounds for another fix round.

security_review.reason: This slice touches migrate.ts's CLI failure-logging sink, a privileged deployment-log surface that can print PostgreSQL/filesystem error content. Requirement is permanent for this slice's scope (migrate.ts/migrate.test.ts), not contingent on any specific measurement, which is why none is restated here -- the current safety properties (provenance-only structured fields, no .message/String(error) ever printed, no credential/path interpolation) are enforced by negative_scope above and proven by packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts's own sink tests directly.

eslint 10's updated eslint:recommended produces a NEW lint error in a file OUTSIDE this slice's declared scope -- report it and HALT, do not fix or silence it
typescript-eslint or @next/eslint-plugin-next turns out to need an upgrade after all when re-measured at execution time -- that widens scope and needs owner authorization

a field currently in SAFE_STRUCTURED_LOG_FIELDS is found to fail the provenance test in a case not yet measured -- that is a design question about the allowlist itself, not a mechanical fix, and needs owner authorization
